nodes.label: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
nodes.description: Central node — Chairman, Drafting Committee; author of the Draft Constitution

nodes.label: Naziruddin Ahmad
nodes.description: Assembly member; raised concern on interpretation of the word 'law'

nodes.label: Mohd. Tahir
nodes.description: Assembly member; raised protection from untouchability concern

nodes.label: Saiyid Jafar Imam
nodes.description: Assembly member; co-raised untouchability protection concern

nodes.label: K. T. Shah
nodes.description: Assembly member; raised Non-segregation of SC/ST and Freedom to the Press points

nodes.label: S. Nagappa
nodes.description: Assembly member; raised access to public places concern

nodes.label: B. G. Kher
nodes.description: Assembly member; co-raised access to public places concern

nodes.label: H. V. Kamath
nodes.description: Assembly member; raised Right to Bear Arms as Fundamental Right

nodes.label: Jaipal Singh
nodes.description: Assembly member; raised Scheduled Tribe terminology and tribal area protections

nodes.label: Sardar Hukam Singh
nodes.description: Assembly member; raised SC/ST unreserved seats, reserved constituencies, minority safeguards

nodes.label: V. I. Muniswamy Pillai
nodes.description: Assembly member; raised population basis for reserved representation

nodes.label: N. C. Laskar
nodes.description: Assembly member; raised reserved constituencies composition

nodes.label: Drafting Committee
nodes.description: Body chaired by Ambedkar responsible for preparing the Draft Constitution.

nodes.label: Government of India Act, 1935
nodes.description: Prior colonial-era legislation whose administrative provisions and Scheduled Tribe enumeration were referenced in drafting the Constitution.

nodes.label: Comparative Federal Models (US & Australia)
nodes.description: American and Australian constitutional/federal structures Ambedkar repeatedly compared India's Draft against, on federalism and amendment procedure.

nodes.label: Introduction of Draft Constitution
nodes.summary: Ambedkar presented the Draft Constitution and explained the work and responsibility of the Drafting Committee.

nodes.label: Form of Government
nodes.summary: Ambedkar explained the form of government proposed in the Draft and distinguished it from presidential systems.

nodes.label: Dual Polity and Single Citizenship
nodes.summary: Ambedkar explained that India would have a dual polity but a single citizenship, without separate State citizenship.

nodes.label: Indian vs American Federalism
nodes.summary: Ambedkar compared India's proposed federal structure with the American model and highlighted differences in Centre-State relations.

nodes.label: Flexible Federalism
nodes.summary: Ambedkar compared the Draft's federal arrangements with Australia's and explained mechanisms intended to reduce excessive rigidity.

nodes.label: Union of States
nodes.summary: Ambedkar explained why India was described as a 'Union' and why States would not possess a right of secession.

nodes.label: Government of India Act provisions
nodes.summary: Ambedkar explained why certain administrative provisions from the 1935 Act were incorporated into the Draft.

nodes.label: Fundamental Rights
nodes.summary: Ambedkar defended the Draft's formulation of Fundamental Rights and its approach to reasonable limitations.

nodes.label: Directive Principles
nodes.summary: Ambedkar explained that Directive Principles were not enforceable by courts but would guide governments and be politically significant.

nodes.label: Constitutional Amendment
nodes.summary: Ambedkar defended the Draft's amendment procedure by comparing it with the more elaborate procedures of other federations.

nodes.label: Interpretation of 'Law'
nodes.summary: Ambedkar responded to Ahmad's concern about the meaning of 'law' and proposed wording to avoid an unintended interpretation.

nodes.label: State Funds & Fundamental Rights
nodes.summary: Ambedkar proposed replacing 'revenues of the State' with 'State funds' so the provision would cover local authorities as well as governments.

nodes.label: Protection from Untouchability
nodes.summary: Ambedkar agreed with the objective of ensuring that untouchable communities could access public places without discrimination, while discussing the legal form of the protection.

nodes.label: Non-segregation of SC/ST
nodes.summary: Ambedkar opposed wording that could allow 'special provisions' to become a basis for segregating Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes from the general public.

nodes.label: Access to public places
nodes.summary: Ambedkar clarified the meaning of 'shop' and related public facilities so that services could not be denied on discriminatory grounds.

nodes.label: Freedom to the Press
nodes.summary: Ambedkar argued that a separate constitutional right for the press was unnecessary because the press exercises the citizen's freedom of expression.

nodes.label: Right to Bear Arms
nodes.summary: Ambedkar opposed making unrestricted possession of arms a Fundamental Right and explained the implications for public administration and security.

nodes.label: Scheduled Tribe Terminology
nodes.summary: Ambedkar explained why 'Scheduled Tribe' was preferred over the broader term 'Adibasi/aboriginal', emphasizing its defined legal meaning.

nodes.label: Legal Definition of Scheduled Tribes
nodes.summary: Ambedkar referred to the earlier use of enumerated communities to give legal meaning to otherwise broad social categories.

nodes.label: Tribal Area Protections
nodes.summary: Ambedkar addressed whether protections attached to a Scheduled Tribe member would continue after migration outside a scheduled or tribal area.

nodes.label: Fundamental Rights & State Restrictions
nodes.summary: Ambedkar defended the Draft's approach of allowing specified limitations on Fundamental Rights rather than treating them as completely absolute.

nodes.label: Reserved Seats for SC/ST
nodes.summary: Ambedkar moved the provision reserving seats for SC/ST in State Legislative Assemblies, with specific treatment for tribal areas of Assam.

nodes.label: SC/ST in Unreserved Seats
nodes.summary: Ambedkar clarified that SC/ST candidates would also be entitled to contest unreserved seats; the matter would be addressed through election law.

nodes.label: Population for Reserved Representation
nodes.summary: Ambedkar discussed how SC/ST population could be estimated for determining reserved representation, including the possibility of a fresh census or voter strength.

nodes.label: Reserved Constituencies
nodes.mentioned: N. C. Laskar / Sardar Hukam Singh
nodes.summary: Ambedkar addressed proposals concerning the composition and territorial arrangement of constituencies containing reserved SC/ST seats.

nodes.label: SC/ST Legislative Representation
nodes.summary: Ambedkar relied on the Assembly's previously accepted Advisory Committee decisions concerning SC/ST representation.

nodes.label: Minority Safeguards
nodes.summary: Ambedkar stated that the Assembly's later decision treated Muslims and Christians differently from SC/ST for the constitutional safeguards under discussion.

nodes.label: Legislative Reservation vs Services
nodes.summary: Ambedkar interpreted the Assembly's decision as removing the relevant privileges from groups no longer treated as minorities under that framework; Hukam Singh challenged whether this extended to services.

nodes.label: Minority Safeguards Monitoring
nodes.summary: Ambedkar proposed a Special Officer responsible for investigating matters relating to constitutional safeguards for minorities and reporting to the President.

nodes.label: Advisory Committee Decisions
nodes.summary: Ambedkar linked the Drafting Committee's amendments to decisions previously reached by the Assembly and Advisory Committee on minority safeguards.
